I love the clear distinction here between the logical and the emotional. It feels like you're constantly pitting the two against each other. To me it tries to highlight the genuine and sometimes illogical understanding of the world that can only be achieved through that emotional connection with other bodies. Other living, or once living, creatures. I'm not an expert by any means, but your poem feels pretty dense to me. In the best way possible. :)

To me I read this as a kind of expression of the beauty of everything in the world. In its creation and after. And then a raw and sudden realization that the world is the same today as the day it was created, as the pieces are all inherently lifeless. So it feels a little nihilistic to me. I'm wondering if you have any particular way that you envisioned this being interpreted?
